rites.name: Pelaldustar
rites.text: Pelaldustar is a concept of the Weave in Nuilleimwen, the thread the makers seed while quiet powers sleep in the Holy Age of flame and temples. It names the pattern by which dormant forces are bound to the orders that will one day wake them.

rites.name: Serones
rites.text: Serones is the concept of the Pact, the oath sworn among the Shards of Nuilleimwen after the Fall, binding fragments of broken worlds into a shared, uneasy order. It is abstract rather than a being, lingering wherever old bonds are tested in the Age of Sundering.

rites.name: Vanatameno
rites.text: Vanatameno is a concept of Nuilleimwen's Walled Age, a principle of holding that the orders of the age built into their walls and temple flames. It was named in the time of first crossings, when wardens sought to keep the old fires from spilling into the wilds.

rites.name: Ryemarleth
rites.text: Ryemarleth is a sigil of dormant ember-glass worn as a lattice across the skin, which awakens to sharpen a single chosen art such as forging, navigation, or song. Its bearer can channel the sigil's stored resonance to shatter weak wards and rattle nearby stone, though the strain eventually burns the lattice away.

rites.name: Miemaenora
rites.text: Miemaenora is a sigil of attentive sight that the Nuilleimwen scholars inscribe upon the eyelids of their investigators, granting an uncanny clarity to whatever the bearer chooses to examine. Its wielders can read the faint residues of past deeds from stone, air, and wounds, and can trace a hidden thread of cause through a crowded city in a single glance.

rites.name: Ilyinelora
rites.text: Ilyinelora is a quiet, lattice-woven sense that lets a bearer feel the resonance of hidden things across distances, tracing them as threads of glowing sound. In the Arcane realm of Nuilleimwen it is considered a gift of seeing rather than of force, and its wielders are sought as cartographers of buried ruins.

rites.name: Alaanneth
rites.text: Alaanneth is a quiet resonance woven through the thornwood groves of Nuilleimwen, a bond that lets its wielder sense the pulse of living things and soothe storms of wild instinct. Its earliest recorded use stilled a river in flood, though the cost to the bearer's own heartbeat was never written down.

rites.name: Elioraneth
rites.text: Elioraneth is a concept of restorative grace woven through the arcane realm of Nuilleimwen during its sixth era, three ages old. Its bearers are said to mend the living by drawing back what has frayed in them, though the mending is never free.

rites.name: Sileirae
rites.text: Sileirae is a quiet theurgical sigil-discipline from the sixth age of Nuilleimwen, practiced by wandering scholars who inscribe thresholds with loops of listening runes. Its adepts can briefly bind the resonance of a city's bells into a single sustained tone, though the strain leaves them mute for days.

rites.name: Lyenaeriel
rites.text: Lyenaeriel is a sigil that channels constructive energy, allowing its bearer to shape matter and weave new forms from the very fabric of reality. When activated, the sigil can mend, forge, and transform objects, landscapes, or even entire celestial bodies with a single thought. Its power is both a tool of creation and a safeguard against destruction, as the bearer can counteract forces that threaten the balance of their world.

rites.name: Ilyima
rites.text: Ilyima is a quiet discipline of threshold-walking in the Nuilleimwen cosmos, a practice in which an initiate learns to cross any boundary, from a shadow to a closed door, by first becoming the crossing itself. Its adepts are known for moving through a crowded market without disturbing a single bell, and for stepping over a ravine as if the ground had simply agreed to continue.

rites.name: Alaarae
rites.text: Alaarae is a quiet cartographer-spirit of Nuilleimwen's Arcane realm, who threads the echoes of spoken vows through tidal ink-wells so that distant promises can be felt as weather. Her hand can stir the currents of the Veil of Assent, but she rarely uses that reach, preferring to keep the sea of spoken oaths calm.

rites.name: Sileira
rites.text: Sileira is a concept of luminous hush-glass that thins the air around its bearer, letting attention stretch across a room like a taut thread. Those who carry it in Nuilleimwen report hearing a candle's breath from across a valley, though the shimmer costs them sleep for weeks afterward. The concept is young and its uses are still being argued over by its two competing schools.

rites.name: Silinniel
rites.text: Silinniel is a concept of the Arcane realm in Nuilleimwen, a binding of dusk-threads that lets a wielder spin shadows into borrowed voices and painted scenes. Its sway is gentle: a sleeping city can be lulled by a lullaby drawn from the dark, and a crowd can be fooled into watching a phantom parade.

rites.name: Nuaruama
rites.text: Nuaruama is a concept of tidal ritual in the Arcane realm of Nuilleimwen, where the sea and the sky agree to hold whoever bears its signs. Those marked by it are cradled by currents when they stumble and can ride the gusts as though they were stairs. Its power is gentle and rarely turns into destruction.

rites.name: Mierla
rites.text: Mierla is a ward-weaving discipline of the Nuilleimwen arcane tradition, practised by bearers who inscribe glyphs of protection over treasures, thresholds, and sleeping cities. Its adepts can hold a sealed doorway against tides of hostile force, though the strain falls heavily on whoever keeps the ward alive.

rites.name: Nuemeth
rites.text: Nuemeth is a shapeshifting discipline practiced in the arcane realm of Nuilleimwen during its sixth era, allowing a practitioner to reshape their outward form as a single deliberate act and return to their birth form at will. Its adepts are forbidden from copying the face of any living soul, a rule enforced by the wardens of the Silver Ledger. Practitioners treat the art as a quiet craft rather than a weapon, though its deeper workings can ripple outward into the surrounding magic of the world.

rites.name: Oriinnys
rites.text: Oriinnys is a hushed arcane discipline in the Nuilleimwen cosmos, practiced by wayfinders who learn to lighten their footing during a sudden sprint. Its adepts glide over rubble, scree, and thorned undergrowth as though the ground had momentarily forgotten to resist them. The art is modest in scope but prized for its quiet efficiency on rough roads.

rites.name: Alaennys
rites.text: Alaennys is a three-year-old arcane concept in the Nuilleimwen omniverse, a lattice of silver resonance that lets the wielder bind any craft tool into a living skill. Its wielders tune their attention until a chosen tool answers them as an old friend would.

rites.name: Lyimiorleth
rites.text: Lyimiorleth is a silver-threaded resonance that hums between the bonded beasts and riders of the Nuilleimwen highlands, letting a handler lend focus to a creature across a wide open field rather than only at arm's reach. It is a concept of the Arcane realm, first recorded in the sixth era, and it remains a quiet art taught only to those who have earned a mount's trust.

rites.name: Miemeirleth
rites.text: Miemeirleth is a veil-weave of quiet sorcery that stitches a performer's presence into the stillness between heartbeats, letting a song or a silent step pass unnoticed by the world's attention. Its practitioners in the drifting reed-cities of Nuilleimwen treat it as both art and camouflage, and it is said to have once hushed an entire tide-bell into silence.

rites.name: Nuamora
rites.text: Nuamora is a quiet sensory art practiced by hunters of the Nuilleimwen drifting marshes, who press a glowing sigil onto the skin to sharpen perception and track their quarry. The mark carries no destructive force of its own, serving only as a lens that draws faint traces of life and motion out of the mist.

rites.name: Veneimilla
rites.text: Veneimilla is a weaving-spirit of the Nuilleimwen arcane courts, bound to threads of memory that it stitches into the minds of those it watches. Its art lets it pin a chosen creature in its thoughts, drawing dreams and dread from that one mind until the pattern unravels.

rites.name: Alaannuamae
rites.text: Alaannuamae is a whispered-cantrip of the Nuilleimwen concept-realm, an instinct of small kindness that a traveler learns in their third age of wandering. It lets its wielder coax a flicker of warmth, a lost thread of song, or a stubborn stain from the world, and it is always spent on someone else's comfort.

rites.name: Venaerlae
rites.text: Venaerlae is a sealed grammar of quiet pressure, drawn by the scholars of Nuilleimwen's third age as a teachable form of unarmed discipline. Its practitioners learn to convert the ordinary weight of a closed hand into a dull, rolling force that bruises stone and bone alike.

rites.name: Elionys
rites.text: Elionys is a silent discipline of the Arcane realm in Nuilleimwen, taught in the E6 era to wanderers who must cross hostile country unseen. Practitioners learn to dissolve their footfalls and breath into the ambient hum of the land, so that a traveler can walk for hours without being heard or noticed. The concept is considered a quiet art rather than a weapon, though its mastery shapes how the wild and the watchful find one another.

rites.name: Eluarys
rites.text: Eluarys is a concept of the Arcane realm in the sixth era of Nuilleimwen, three ages old, a quiet pattern that lets the bearer knot ordinary reeds, ash, and river clay into a fleeting charm. The charm dissolves at dusk, leaving only a faint scent of woodsmoke behind.

rites.name: Ryireina
rites.text: Ryireina is a silver-threaded sigil-binding of the Arcane realm, born in the sixth era of Nuilleimwen, that lets a practitioner tie a single nearby soul to their own will for a stretch of time. Its bindings are said to pull the marked one's stored strength toward the caster, sometimes with enough force to fracture stone.

rites.name: Miarora
rites.text: Miarora is a concept of quiet inheritance, a stillness that clings to abandoned vaults and sealed reliquaries in the Nuilleimwen Arcane era. Scholars of the third age say it lets a careful mind read the echoes of old mechanisms, letting it sense where a ward has thinned and where a cog of memory still turns.

rites.name: Alailaena
rites.text: Alailaena is a sealed binding-art in the Nuilleimwen omniverse, a ceremonial rite that lets a seeker sense the scattered living things across a hushed valley, but only when performed slowly with full ritual. Its practitioners guard it jealously, for it reveals where every creature and sprout lies without ever granting the power to move them.

rites.name: Nuerluamwen
rites.text: Nuerluamwen is a concept of hushed bargains in the Arcane realm of Nuilleimwen, where the Third Age of the Sixth Era shaped it into a quiet hinge between thought and speech. Its nature is to sway the minds of those who hear it, reshaping conviction without a single raised voice.

rites.name: Ryemeth
rites.text: Ryemeth is a tenth-age arcane sigil-craft that binds a bearer's dread into a ringing word of command. When spoken among the wardens of Nuilleimwen, the word makes unshielded minds bow before the speaker's gaze.

rites.name: Miirora
rites.text: Miirora is a resonant veil of woven silence that drapes over gatherings of listeners, turning every spoken word into a glowing thread. Its bearers draw on it to command attention, letting their voices bend a crowd's mood as easily as wind bends grass.

rites.name: Nuariel
rites.text: Nuariel is a conceptual sigil-current that hums through the Nuilleimwen arcane realm, binding listeners to the cadence of whatever they are trying to convince. Its influence is strongest in the third age of the realm, when speakers learned to braid its resonance into their arguments.

rites.name: Nuiriel
rites.text: Nuiriel is a concept of quiet sensing in the Nuilleimwen cosmos, a practice that reads hidden auras and toxins only through slow, deliberate rites. Its practitioners trace the faint signatures of enchantment and blight across a room, bound by patience rather than instant insight.

rites.name: Miemioneth
rites.text: Miemioneth is a quiet arcane concept in the Nuilleimwen omniverse, a ward-thread woven from the third age's oldest practice of hardened meditation. It holds a single protective weave that refreshes itself only after its bearer completes a long, deliberate rest.

rites.name: Alaanwen
rites.text: Alaanwen is a cantrip-like tuning of the Nuilleimwen arcane spheres, a weave of softened glamour that bends what observers perceive without touching what is real. Its wielders, drawing on their presence rather than their study, can wear a passing illusion over a room for a short while.

rites.name: Elaelirys
rites.text: Elaelirys is a veil-stepping art of the Arcane realm in Nuilleimwen, where practitioners slip across short gaps of air by folding the space they can see. Its masters can shear a stone pillar clean through by cutting the seam of their own fold. The art is taught quietly and only to those patient enough to master short distances first.

rites.name: Silinneth
rites.text: Silinneth is a veil-weaver of the Nuilleimwen arcane reaches, three centuries into the Sixth Era, who learned to slip from sight by folding the listener's attention rather than shadow. Her works are said to have quieted a drowning moon-tide so the tide-wardens could not hear the ocean's call. Her lineage still guards the hidden gates of the western Choirs.

rites.name: Silemiorys
rites.text: Silemiorys is a veil-thread of old arcane craft in Nuilleimwen, woven to soak up the crackling storms that roll through the Arcane realm. Its bearers grow hardened to the sky's fury, able to bleed off lightning that would wither lesser mages.

rites.name: Nuerora
rites.text: Nuerora is a sigil-tuned resonance in the Arcane realm of Nuilleimwen, a concept that lets a bearer's stride quicken as the ground answers their footfall. It was woven in the third age of the Sixth Era, when mages first learned to bind minor kinetic grace into permanent glyphs.

rites.name: Venuallora
rites.text: Venuallora is a quiet discipline in the Arcane realm of Nuilleimwen, taught in the sixth age as a way of bending another's aim away from its mark. Practitioners learn to weave a thread of doubt through a hostile gaze at the instant it strikes, so the blow goes wide. It is a defense of attention rather than of flesh.

rites.name: Veneirys
rites.text: Veneirys is a veil-dweller of the Arcane realm of Nuilleimwen, an aspect of endurance that the Sixth Era's loom-wardens wove into a single resilient thread. Its kind stands against spells that would unravel the mind or body, and it is said to outlast the tearing of stars.

rites.name: Veneinora
rites.text: Veneinora is a sealed concept of thought-binding that lets a speaker lodge a whispered line inside the listener's memory, to be heard again only at the moment the bearer chooses. In the Nuilleimwen arcane courts of the sixth era, it is taught as a humble craft of clerks and envoys rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Oriinniel
rites.text: Oriinniel is a quiet mnemonic lattice woven through the Nuilleimwen cloudforges, awakened by the careful hands of tide-pilots and sky-riggers. It stores the steadying rhythms of skilled craft and returns them to whoever tunes it, lending a tremor of unexpected grace to their work.
